Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed head-on collision with neck pain, stiffness, and headaches consistent with whiplash-type
cervical strain. The mechanism of injury is well matched to the reported symptoms and the force involved in the crash. Cervical
range of motion was reduced on examination, with paraspinal tenderness and muscle guarding noted at each visit. Imaging
findings clearly confirm the soft-tissue injury, and there is no known prior injury to the cervical spine or surrounding structures.
Consrevative care was provided, including manual therapy, stretching and srtengthening exercises, and modalities for pain
control. Over eighteen visits the patient improved steadily, though recovery took somewhat longer than is typical for this injury.
Treatment billing reflects single charges for each service rendered, with no repeated or duplicate entries. Ongoing home exercise
instruction was provided, and the patient was advised to return if symptoms worsen or new neurological signs develop.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

  spelling errors as they are,
